items.note: Cause: tour.js place(). Its four places beside the lit area checked only one end of each place against the screen. The top place needs the card's top inside the screen, but not its bottom. In landscape the step's anchor (the shape list in the More tools sheet) is below the screen. v16.3's two new tiles moved it 54 px lower (613 to 667 px), so the place above it moved off the screen too and no longer touched the sheet's window. place() took it, and the card went below the screen. In v16.2 that place overlapped the window by luck, so place() fell back to the bar. Fix: each side place must lie inside the screen at both ends. With nothing else free, a phone gets the one-line bar again. Unit tests (t_tour, 1330/1330, 4 new): the gate's case at 780 x 360 gives the bar; with no bar the card stays inside the screen; an anchor above the screen too; a fuzz of 6000 anchors off the screen keeps the card inside. The 4 new checks fail on v16.3's tour.js, and that run gives the gate's own card (401, 367). Browser (acc/land_shapes.json, shots/): basics/shapes shows the bar at the top in all 4 configs (780 x 360 and 844 x 390, en and ru). v16.3 still puts the card below the screen in 3 of them, and v16.2 shows the bar. tour_phone_cmd, full run: outOfView 0 (gate 3). Bars rise from 187 to 190, which are these 3 steps. Everything else equals the gate: 348 steps, 0 over the work area, 0 touches blocked, tries 5/5, race, rotate, fold and urlbar OK, 0 exceptions. tour_cmd 97/97, tour_lit 88/88. Tour audit, 24 configs: 1056 step views, 0 failing. Layers 384/0, follow 56/0, focus 24/0. The app findings are the gate's 10 (basics/shapes at 1024, edit/zp at 390 ru touch).

constr.js perpForm has a new exact rule for a curve C through three points: a 3-point circle, or an arc. Its centre and radius are not decimals (the circle through 0, 1, i has r = 0.7071...), but its form is rational in the points. With the points, P and Q as 12-digit decimals scaled to integers, it tests both parts of A u conj(v) + (D - iE) u / 2 + (D + iE) conj(v) / 2 = 0 exactly. Here u = P - p1, v = Q - p1, and A, D, E are circle3's own coefficients, anchored at p1. True means the pencil. The circle3 node keeps its points on its form (G.p3), which a flip does not drop. Collinear points (a line) are covered too. The rule is skipped when the decimals and the form disagree on A = 0 (collinear by incidence). Result: on the circle through 0, 1, i, the binary pair 1+0.5i & 1.5+0.5i and six decimal mirror pairs all give the pencil, as drawn and flipped. So do a circle with centre 0.3-0.2i, collinear points on y = x, and the arc through 0, 1, i. Near misses stay the line or a circle. v16.3 gave the line through the centre for the decimal pairs: all six on the circle through 0, 1, i, the 0.3-0.2i circle, and the arc. The binary pair and the y = x pair were already the pencil. The pairs are in t_constr section E (constr_perp_tests.js, 3 new checks): A 66, B 18, C 54, D 26, E 51, F 39, 254/254. constr_cmd 115/115, perp_cmd 79/79, touch_cmd 90/90, fix163 20/20. Not covered: a C that is itself a perpendicular or touching circle. Its form comes from other shapes, not from decimals, so it keeps only the exact binary test.

construct.js on() remembers a 'loadFreed' that arrives before the app's adapter. ui(A) then shows the toast 'Some constructions could not be read and were opened as plain shapes.' A link or scene file is freed by openFigure before the reload, so that toast was lost. app.js now passes ':freed' with cmw-opened, and the toast after the reload says both: 'Opened the figure from the link. Some constructions could not be read and were opened as plain shapes.' The strings already had Russian entries; make_ru_table --strict: 2370 entries, 0 unresolved, i18n_ru.js unchanged. acc/toast_check.json uses a figure with an op from a later build ('future2'). Saved: the toast shows in en and ru, and the shape is a plain circle. Link: the combined toast shows. v16.3 shows no toast for the saved figure, and only 'Opened the figure from the link.' for the link.

construct.js syncChip: when the chip would wrap, it drops ' · Esc cancels' if that keeps it on one line. If it still wraps, the whole text stays on two lines (or the shorter text, when the whole one would be cut at two). The chip is measured only when its text or the plane's width changes. acc/chip_check.json and shots/chip-*, at 1440 x 900 (X 427 px wide): the touching circle's chip after P' and after the ring's tangent now reads 'Touching point on Circle 1, or a ring for a tangent · Touching' on one line (353 px). v16.3 used two lines, with 'cancels' alone on the second. In Russian, the Orthogonal tool's first chip is now one line, 'Выберите прямую или окружность · Ортогональная'. v16.3 used two lines. The Russian rings chip does not fit one line even without Esc, so it keeps the whole text on two full lines, as before. All other first chips (6 tools, en and ru) are unchanged, with Esc. Three test expectations were updated for this: perp_cmd C RU chip, touch_cmd A5 and fix163 U6. They now accept the one-line form only when it is one line.

items.status: rejected with evidence (predates v16; no app change)
items.note: The task was not reproduced in 20 videos made here (acc/video_lt.json, video_lt_throttle.json): plane 1920x1080 60 fps and globe 1080x1080, on v16.3.1 and on v15.2.1, each with a CPU profile, also with CPU throttling at 3x. The longtask observer reported no task in any of them. The profiles show the same work on both builds. One stretch is the first frame: gl.js begin grows the shared GL canvas to the video size, 22-32 ms, next to pickEncoder or videoPlan. The other stretches are GC and native work, 50-74 ms in total, spread over several tasks (v15.2.1 globe: GC 35 + native 32 ms). makeVideo and videoPlan are byte-identical to v15.2.1's. videoFrame differs by one line, the ranged deformation's start boundary. History of this check in 12 export runs: one long task in v16.1+user-5 run 1 (globe 58 ms) and one in the v16.2 merge (plane 80 ms, load 17). The same check on the preview path failed in the v15.2 patch run (83 ms). The other 10 runs, the v15.2, v16 and v16.3 gates among them, had none. So the task predates v16. It depends on load, and its stretches are engine GC and the first frame's canvas growth, not one splittable task. Proposal, not made: pre-grow the GL canvas in its own task before the first frame (gl.js), if the user wants it.

Cause: the long-press tip (app.js). A touch on a view button starts a 450 ms timer, and when the timer fires first the release swallows the click. The timer runs on the page's clock. If the page is busy (a page still settling), the timer can run before the pending release, even for a 60 ms tap. Reproduced (acc/land_tap.json, land_tap_A.json): a 60 ms tap on Landscape at 390 x 844, with the page's main thread busy for 700, 1200 or 2000 ms right after the touch starts, is lost 6 of 6 times on v16.3. It takes at 0 and 300 ms. Fix: the release decides by the events' own times (pointerdown.timeStamp, pointerup.timeStamp). A release less than 450 ms after the press is a tap: the tip goes and the click goes through. v16.3.1: 10 of 10 taps take, busy 0 to 2000 ms. A real 700 ms press on an idle page still shows the tip 'Landscape of F3' and does not switch the view, on both builds (acc/lp_long.json). The smoke's own sequence (the section-8 state, tap 600 to 3600 ms after opening): 24 of 24 take on both builds.

items.note: The gate could not confirm any perf failure as a v16.3 regression and proposed a re-run on a quiet machine. This patch changes the tour's placement, the chip's text, a toast, the long-press decision and an exact test on perpendicular circles. None of these is in a measured render path. The perf suite was not re-run, and no baseline or accepted entry was touched. The proposal stands.

items.status: open, not a v16.3.1 regression (same on v16.3)
items.note: The release smoke failed one check in ru 1440 dark, 'More formats opens over the dialog', in 2 of 3 runs. Its other 7 configs passed, as did the third run (33/33). Section 9 alone, alternated 6 times per build (acc/more_formats.json): the menu fails to open 3 of 6 times on v16.3.1 and 3 of 6 on v16.3. Cause: the Export figure dialog is still growing when the smoke finds its More formats button ready. The button moves about 42 px down (y 767 to 809), so the click lands on the dialog body. A quick user could miss it the same way. The app was not changed for this. Possible fixes: the smoke waits for the dialog's size to settle, or the dialog keeps its footer still while it fills.
